Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: OrderMate portal activation handshake failing — quick assist needed

Hi Elena,

We pushed your supplier invite through our Coupa integration this morning (PO: PO-93842) and I’m seeing your team click the activation link but land on a page that says “no token found / session not initialized.”

I attached the onboarding checklist we sent initially — can you confirm a couple quick things so we can triage:
- Which browser and OS did you try (Chrome/Safari/Edge + version)?
- Did anyone try in an incognito/private window or on a different network?
- Is the session error happening for multiple users at your org or just one person (if multiple, please provide a couple of emails).

I’ve cc’d Monica (onboarding) and Ben (support escalation) so they can join the remediation if it’s a backend handshake.

If you can reply with the screenshot and approximate time when you clicked the link, we’ll correlate with server logs. I’ve also attached the original onboarding-instructions-ordermate.pdf for reference.

Apologies for the inconvenience — we’ll get this sorted quickly.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T12:03:15-08:00
Subject: RE: OrderMate portal activation handshake failing — quick assist needed

Thanks for the notes, Vivek and Elena.

Quick triage summary from my side after looking at the screenshot and comparing server logs (correlated to the timestamp Elena sent):
- The invite click reaches our relay endpoint but the RelayState param is occasionally empty for links routed through the Coupa redirector.
- When RelayState is missing, our session service falls back to the token cookie; if the cookie is absent (some enterprise browsers strip third-party cookies) you see the "no token present" page.
- We've seen similar behavior when the invite is opened from an embedded browser (mobile app/webview) or when a proxy strips query params.

Short-term remediation I recommend:
1) Resend the invite from the supplier portal but also add a manual claim code in the email body so users can redeem it at /supplier/claim instead of relying on link params. I’ve drafted the manual-claim-instructions.txt attached — please include that text in the resend.
2) Ask OrderMate to try the invite from a laptop on a network without a proxy (we know they tried guest Wi‑Fi, but some corporate proxies do similar stripping).
3) I will open an internal ticket for engineering (INF-7823) to add server-side tolerant parsing (treat missing RelayState as a valid flow if a short-lived fallback token exists).

Ben — can you prepare a resend and make sure the email contains the manual claim code line (example: CLAIM-ORD-6K92) and log the new invite id so we can trace the next click?

If that fails, we can escalate to a quick phone debug with OrderMate and engineering on the call.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Supplier Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: manual-claim-instructions.txt (TXT, 2KB)

Hi Elena — I resent a fresh invite just now and added a manual claim code in the body as Monica suggested. The claim code is: CLAIM-ORD-6K92.

Steps for you:
1) Open the invite email in your regular mailbox (not forwarded).
2) If clicking the link again shows the "no token present" page, go to https://portal.redwood.com/supplier/claim and paste the claim code above.
3) If that still fails, please call my cell at +1 (415) 555‑0182 and I’ll start a live session with engineering on standby.

I logged the new invite id and linked it to INF-7823 in our ticketing system so Monica and engineering can trace it.

Apologies for the friction — I’ll stay on this until you’re activated.

—Ben
